citations.excerpt: US30303M1027,META,2026-05-05,NAME_CHANGE,1,1,,FB,META,Facebook Inc. renamed Meta Platforms Inc.; ticker FB changed to META

detail.description: Facebook Inc. renamed Meta Platforms Inc.; ticker FB changed to META
detail.position_reconciles: yes - quantity, price and cost basis all agree

breaks.narrative: Meridian Securities is still reporting Meta Platforms Inc. under the ticker FB. It became META on 2026-05-05. The position itself is correct — yes - quantity, price and cost basis all agree — because the line was matched on CUSIP 30303M102 rather than on the ticker, and the identifier did not change. Nothing is misstated. What is stale is the security master, and a ticker is how two systems agree they are discussing the same instrument. Tickers are reissued to unrelated companies, and on the day this one is, the match stops being harmless. Sources: corporate_actions_2026Q2.csv:7, meridian_positions_2026-06-30.csv:14.
breaks.proposed_fix: Ask Meridian Securities when their security master was last refreshed against the reference feed. Treat the answer as the finding: a ticker four weeks stale usually means unapplied corporate actions are sitting behind it, and those do move money. Confirm any downstream system that matches on ticker rather than ISIN or CUSIP.

rules_run.checks: Opening quantity plus every booked movement must equal closing quantity.
A holding that left the statement must be accounted for by the activity file.
Every corporate action in the reference feed must be applied by every custodian.
An applied action must move the share count by the declared ratio.
A split divides basis per share and leaves the total unchanged.
Both legs of a merger must be processed: target removed, acquirer credited.
A custodian must not report a security under a superseded ticker.
A statement's converted values must agree with the rates it prints.
Cost basis rolled through the period's activity must match what is reported.
Two custodians reporting one mandate must report the same share count, once both are put on the same statement basis.
Custodians reporting one mandate must be compared on one statement basis.
Two custodians must price the same instrument alike on the same date.
A fee charged in the prior period must recur or be explained.
